item.title: Impossibly possible (greenlight wanted)
item.description: A certain probability
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): containment procedure (none) and then description, followed by multiple attempts at using the number.

Elevator Pitch: a specific probability range, when the conditions are reached becomes certain. For example, if you flipped a penny “the number” amount of times, you would reach your desired result. The “certain result” is decided by the intention of the system.

Central Narrative: A foundation researcher discovering the number through the first moon landing and several tests. The foundation then attempts to utilize it in multiple ways to contain SCPs.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the SCP is an effect, not an object
Additional Notes: thanks for input in advance

item.title: A Balkan fairy tail
item.description: Seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History

Page Layout (Optional): The article is made out of several camera and audio footages.

Elevator Pitch: The story is set in the Bosnian war. A girl with powers of a fairy is found in Bosnia. The Balkan MTF force captures her. Agent Kosta, an ethnic Croat born in Canada is sent to recover her but the Balkan base is atacked by the Chaos insurgency. The battle ends with Kosta and one insurgent as the only survivors. Kosta grabs the girl and they go through the war torn Bosnia, trying to reach the Croatian coast while runing from the still alive insurgent.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: As they drive through Bosnia, Kosta starts to bond with the kid. The child doesn't speak but communicates with Kosta by creating pictures on the various surfaces with her fairy dust. They meet various individuals from all three sides of the Bosnian conflict. In an abandoned coffy bar "Amsterdam", where all of the ethnicities laugh and drink together, while the girl, now going by the name Bojana Skadaric, plays with the other kids, he gets drunk and tells the sad fate of his wife, and how he lost her in a mission. His best friend Sam blamed him for her loss and they never saw each other again. The insurgent atacks the pub and destroys it. They reach an area controled by a Croatian warlord "Swedish" that commands a volunteer division while the local offical army unwillingly follows his orders. Swedish is in a blood feud with a local Serbian warlord. He finds out about the fairy abilities of the girl, as she intervened in an execution, but before he could capture her the Serbs start an offensive and the Serbian commander challenges Swedish to come out. Enraged, Swedish leads the volunteers to battle. The leader of the official army realises that his commander went completely insane, and orders the evacuation of the village. Kosta and Bojana go to the evacuation truck and is stoped by the voice of the chaos insurgent who calls Kosta by name, it is Sam. As he leaves to confront his former friend he tells the army leader to go far away with Bojana. He and Sam have only one bulet each and as they fire at each other a bomb drops between them, ending the footage.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is about old conflicts that were never resolved coming to light. Bojana represents a generation not bound to those conflicts and has a future that she can choose freely, while Kosta, Sam and the people of Bosnia are chained to their fate.

item.title: Twinportation
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A set of twin beds that allow teleportation in between them. Sleeping in one bed will cause you to wake up in the other, regardless of distance between the two. The sleeper feels no change during the night, and cameras and surveillance of the bed during transport show the sleeper just vanishing.

Central Narrative: None.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A bed used by the foundation to transport quickly across long distances.

Additional Notes: Not an extremely deep entry, but I just think it sounds good.

item.title: Cannibalism Cantaloupes - Seeking Greenlights
item.description: Melons that force you the eat them, and once you do others will be coming for your head (literally)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): In addition to the SCP and description an incident report with video log and an interview with someone present during the incident

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a bunch of melon plants that compel people to eat them through a cognitohazard. Once they've been eaten a similar effect is placed on the head of the person who ate the melon, where other people will chase you to the ends of the earth in order to eat your brains, nose, eyes and all that good stuff.
Edit: The effect does not transfer to those who ate the infected person, but a new plant wil grow out of their skull after a couple weeks, killing them in the process.

Central Narrative: One of the members of the team that went to retrieve the SCP was pulled in by its effect and then eaten by the rest of their team members. The video log in the incident report and interview will show two perspectives on the horrors that unfolded, with the log showing an objective perspective and the interview a hazy and traumatized perspective.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's very much inspired by zombie stories, at least the part where your friends become the monsters you have to fight.

Additional Notes: I'm new to writing these articles and don't know every object on the site, so I don't know if this sort of stuff is something that's been done to death

item.title: Idea: Intertemporal Boots (Stay With Me Here)
item.description: A pair of boots that causes the user to move through space normally, but also allows them to walk through time so to speak.
item.content:encoded:
The SCP is a pair of boots. They would either be made from cloth and have a magical 'Serpent's Hand' sort of feel, or be completely robotic/futuristic. The file would go over the basic mechanics of the boots and testing would include D-Class being thrown throughout various time periods only to have the Foundation return them via some sort of temporal anchor.

Nothing crazy at first, walking forward on the x and z axis causes the user to jump forward in time. Walking backward on the x and z-axis causes them to jump backward in time. The file should get weirder when the D-Class starts moving on the y-axis. This segment would be heavily redacted/classified, but I think the file should imply that the D-Class is visiting other timelines that lay parallel to our own. (It's this part were I would need the most help on brainstorming ideas.)

Just an idea, but it would be a real hoot to write. I'm aiming for more of a Series I/II feel with this article. Nothing world-ending about this SCP, just some anomalous dimension shifting.

item.title: Emergent Ego (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: read certain SCP files in a particular order, and become possessed by some unknown personality that emerges and overwhelms your own personality.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Sci-Fi / Esoteric

Elevator Pitch: Exposure to particular combinations of SCP files, or the knowledge therein, results in the emergence of deviant archetypal personalities with anomalous properties, which override the ego of the subject viewing the files; read certain SCP files, and become possessed by some unknown personality.

Central Narrative: Discovered when a Class-B staff member experienced a psychological break accompanied by anomalous change in personality, physiology, and working esoteric knowledge; review of foundation records revealed a similar incident in the past.

The only known commonality between the incidents is the exposure to a particular set of case files over a period of six months. These files, known in combination as [SCP Number]-1, represent one of possibly numerous patterns that cause archetypal emergence.

In the case of [SCP Number]-1, the emergence of the accompanying personality was retroactively associated with a number of symptoms prior to complete ego eclipse. These all occur prior to the full emergence of the archetypical personality. A psychological profile of the emergent personality is nonetheless included based on the data available.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Research ongoing: one D-Class personnel is to be exposed to the pattern of SCP files to try and replicate an emergence event. In addition, Foundation researchers, aided by onsite supercomputers, are parsing incident reports for similar commonalities to indicate additional patterns and corresponding archetypes.

Additional Notes: This SCP is meant to serve a dual purpose, as a frame story for an SCP podcast that I'm working on — I want to be up front that this is ultimately my intention, but I still fully believe that the idea can stand alone as an entry, and in no way am I trying to create a subpar SCP just to enable a related venture. My primary goal is to make this SCP happen, and, should it be approved and see some success, I'll then explore additional creative avenues with it.

The podcast will be from the perspective of the D-Class personnel being exposed to articles (under the pretense of reading and recording them for accessibility use within the Foundation). The D-Class in question will slowly deteriorate into this emergent personality over the course of the podcast, as a part of the overarching narrative.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight- The Book of Omens
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Green light: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Elevator Pitch:A photo album that can predict disasters and death.
Central Narrative: A long explanation of how the photo album works. It shows photos of a woman in various places, from various time periods. Depending on how long the viewer has to live, the woman will appear to be a different age. The places she appears in the photos are sites of famous disasters shortly before they happened, such as 9/11 or Chernobyl. The article ends with the writer speculating they could use the book to predict containment breaches or disasterous experiments by having their personnel look at the book, but then there's an addendum. A new photo has appeared in the book, and the background is the SCP site it's being held in.
Hook: Through the course of the story, the book seems relatively harmless (if a little disturbing) but some things, like the name of the site it's held at, are redacted for unclear reasons. Then at the end, why it was redacted becomes clear, and it raises whole new questions about the true nature of the book and the future.
Additional notes: This might be more a question for full draft editing, but I'm not sure whether to spice it up with more speculations or hints about how dangerous the book actually is, or whether to keep it more passive or mysterious. (Adding notes from one researcher to another, test logs, etc.)

item.title: Eurotrash
item.description: A UIU Tale idea, Greenlights 0 of 2
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Action/Adventure, maybe a touch of horror

Page Layout (Optional): Normal story stuff

Elevator Pitch: The UIU encounters The Aristocrats (SCP 3288)

Central Narrative: When Emperor Maximilian I went to Mexico to take the throne, whether knowingly or not, a collection of his "cousins" came with him. While they've managed to fly relatively below the radar until now, a series of disappearances and particularly gruesome recovered bodies along the US/Mexico border have sparked interest.
When a cell phone is recovered with one of the bodies, and holds a picture of what might be a "malformed humanoid" a detachment from the UIU is sent to take over the investigation, as the situation still seems within the wheelhouse of the UIU, or at least no other shadowy groups appear to take it out of their hands.
Investigation leads to battle with a branch of SCP 3288, who's leader believes themselves to be "Sovereign of all North America" with possible implications that by this point they've spread well past the local area.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An old fashioned "monster battle" adventure story with the Bureau.

Additional Notes: Phone posted, so this is especially abbreviated.

item.title: It Will Not Leave
item.description: A grieved MTF officer cannot let his dead squadmate go
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Interviews and incident logs to be included.

Elevator Pitch: : An MTF officer starts to spot in random situations a former squad companion who died in an earlier Containment operation. Despite Foundation help with amnestics, the visions become more frequent and intense.

Central Narrative: Adam and Samuel have been friends since nursery times: they attended the same high school and joined the police academy at the same time. After some time in a police station, they are recruited by the SCP Foundation to join a MTF. Some years later, during a Containment operation, Samuel fails to follow protocol and ends up with Adam dead. The grief and sense of guilt pursuits Samuel to the point that starts to see Adam during his routine more often with time, to the point that jeopardizes other companions during some MTF operations. After a psychological test, he is given an amnestic to forget about his friend and stick to the MTF. However, after some time without issues, during an intense MTF operation, Samuel provokes a containment breach as he claims that an unknown individual appeared to him. This appearance will never leave from then on. After providing a description to the psychologist, matching that of Adam, he is given another amnestic. The entity does not disappear though, and it starts to directly intervene in Adam’s actions, deterring him from any basic activity. Foundation demotes him and keeps him a study subject, classifying Adam’s apparition as an SCP object. Eventually, Samuel commits suicide. An MTF operative from Samuel’s former MTF squad is recorded in a tapped phone call claiming that he has spotted Samuel in his garden and is afraid of reporting this to the Foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Adam’s apparition to Samuel is not real. It is driven by strong feelings of guilt, grief and melancholy. The abnormality comes from the exaggerated expression of these feelings, which get so stuck to Samuel and his subconscious that even amnestics cannot fully support Samuel. In benefit of maintaining resources, rather than promoting an adequate mental health, Foundation classifies it as an anomaly and moves on. Samuel’s sorrow becomes a memetic effect.

Additional Notes: There are two main ideas that I wanted to explore. First, how even long-term friendship can deeply mark an individual; and second, the HRM policy of the Foundation regarding its MTF operatives, and the perils of mental health mismanagement.

item.title: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.description: This is the current deletions thread.
item.content:encoded:
All Staff-enacted Deletions are carried out according to the Deletions Guide.

Summary deletions result for:

  • Articles with malicious intent
  • Pages that are clearly unfinished.
  • Attempts to "game" site procedure, such as re-posting a non-rewritten article in an attempt to get around downvotes.
  • Blatantly plagiarized material.
  • An article posted outside of the current range.

If an author attempts to self-delete their work and fails to do so properly, including either by blanking the page or renaming it, it will be deleted properly by Staff.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.description: Have you joined the site because you're an avid reader and are planning to vote, comment, or just lurk on the site? Interested in helping develop the Next Best Thing? Post your introduction here!
item.content:encoded:
Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, readers and reviewers of the Foundation Universe!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

Let's start off with some things to take a look at to enhance your reading, now that you're a site member:

  • If you have any questions about the Foundation'verse and its various individuals and groups of interest, head over to the Foundation Universe forum to talk about the various aspects of living/working/being in constant fear of a world where anomalies are real.
  • Did you know our site has a night mode version? If you're interested in that (and a few other neat things!), check out our Usertools page.
  • Want to leave a comment or read others' thoughts on something you've read recently? Scroll down to the bottom of that page you read, click the "Discuss" link, and take a look at the comments others have posted!

For those looking to put your knowledge of the SCP-verse to work and contribute to the site by helping develop works-in-progress, head on over to the Writing Help forums!

  • So you want to be a concept reviewer?
  • So you want to be a draft reviewer?
  • And of course, remember the Criticism Policy!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Go ahead and respond to other new members if you find that your interests overlap, and definitely ask for reading suggestions if there's a particular kind of SCP article or tale you enjoy reading. If you're looking to get started as a critiquer, feel free to mention the kind of material you particularly want to see more of on the wiki! You might even see some of our authors drop by here from time to time, if you mention you liked their work! :)

Welcome to the site!

Hello, prospective site writers! It's good to see you here!

First off, a couple standard things to keep in mind as you get started towards adding your voice to the Foundation universe:

Feel free to respond to other new members if you find that your writing interests and/or plans overlap. The SCP wiki is a collaborative writing community, after all! You might even see some of the longtime writers here drop by with comments now and then. :)

item.title: The Candy Cane
item.description: Sounds a little corny but I had this idea since Thanksgiving so I decided to try it out.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror and History

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: The SCP I envisioned is a plastic candy cane filled with small M&M-like candies that have different outcomes to it. While one candy that was eaten will give a person something like a lost possession or make them feel happy another could have immense tragedy or have the person who ate it either die or vanish through a trans dimensional entry way or property while a small select few saying that they are speaking for the candy cane.

Central Narrative: The story is mainly about how the candies affected history and while they test the object it shows some form of sentience and claims to have caused some of the worst tragedies and triumphs in history and saying that they had been the first thing consumed and will be the last thing consumed by man.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is just an idea that I had and wanted to share. While some SCP’s are intriguing for their gruesome nature and such I think an SCP that is more based on luck and a way to solve some of the worlds greater mysteries and why certain things happened would be a intriguing idea.

Additional Notes: I just have a problem of answering a genre. However, I am pretty confident in this even with a hiccup in that department. I will except all the feedback I can get because this one I want to see through till the end and make this my first SCP entry.

item.title: SCP-5233
item.content:encoded:
Big big big thanks to my lovely reviewers in chat: Pratten, Savan, Calibri_Bold, Mars, chaucer345, and Karakatt for all your wonderful suggestions to better develop the backstory here!

Image source is here: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Common_earwig_(Forficula_auricularia)_on_thumb.jpg

Notes:
- All of Wiggy’s interview excerpt dialogue consists of words found in the Wikipedia article for Earwig: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earwig
- Why earwigs? 1. When I was in elementary school, my friends and I found a very large pincher bug on the playground and admired it. Some other kid picked it up and tore off its pincers to keep as a souvenir. That image has stuck with me for over a decade. I can’t smush earwigs anymore. Also last month I found one in a box at work the other day and I let him go outside and it reminded me of that incident. 2. Quoth Wikipedia, “Earwigs are among the few non-social insect species that show maternal care.” Pinchy pinch moms are good moms. There’s a lot of neat facts about earwigs.
- Why Arizona? During my background research, I found this: https://cals.arizona.edu/yavapai/anr/hort/byg/archive/earwig.html so I just went with Arizona.

Best wishes to everyone in this crazy year. To everyone who has the opportunity to nurture a life, no matter how small, and those who teach others to do the same, you are the hope of the world.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Drama

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid SCP that is approximately from 6 to 15 feet tall, dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, and has its general appearance as a tall black figure that has devoid facial features, and no sign of hair, nose, eyes, has unchecked limitations, and numerous of anomalous abilities. In all of which, it is in foundation custody. The Foundation's goal was to prevent its anomalous abilities from attempting to cause out an event of containment breaches by accident. The containment procedure was to keep SCP-XXXX inside a 16 x 60 ft (about 3.7 x 5.5m) room constructed out of tungsten.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid entity dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, comprised of a white shirt, a black or red tie, black trousers, and black shoes. It measures 6 to 15 feet tall has a general appearance as a tall black figure. However, it is possible that this is not SCP-XXXX's true form and that it is an eldritch being that cannot comprehend whose proper form. Its face is pitch black, utterly devoid of facial features. However, despite lacking facial features, SCP-XXXX can sense when its targets are near at all times, as it never hesitates and always sees the targets around it. SCP-XXXX has various anomalous abilities that the Foundation was to yet discovered. The ones learned so far are based on the logs of the incident, description, experiments, and interviewing logs of the Foundation, which are:

+ show block
– hide block
  • Teleportation.
  • Mind-affecting.
  • Memory adding, erasing, and inhibiting.
  • Causing instant death by making eye contact with a subject longer than three (3) seconds.
  • Extremely high superhuman attributes.
  • Causing out technological disruption upon technologies in random times without wanting it to do so.
  • Able to sense how dangerous the ones it confronts are.
  • Cause out phenomenons to become omnipresent and warp space and time between locations.
  • Strong regenerative healing factor.
  • SCP-XXXX's skin causes out common diseases that could lead to the death of those who touch it.
  • Able to sprout out tendrils that're sustainable towards all harmful things in any place of its body.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of having an SCP that has various extremely dangerous and powerful anomalous abilities.

Additional Notes: I couldn't figure it out. People said that my grammar was having problems, but I've fixed my grammar errors and even improved my SCP article. What am I really missing?


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: First Time Author looking for review
item.description: essentially a voodoo doll, but bear with me, there's a twist
item.content:encoded:
At first glance it might seem boring, my idea is essentially a voodoo doll, but bear with me, there's a twist that I think is unique enough to give this a chance. I've been reading SCPs for years and I've always wanted to write my own but I usually scrap them because I don't think they're good enough, so I'm really excited to share this :)

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: voodoo doll that when picked up, causes the subject to fly into rage against the last person to anger them, the voodoo doll will take on the appearance of that person, and the subject will use it to kill the victim by any means available. These people are now known as SCP-XXX-1(Subject) and -2(victim). When the victim is killed, the doll reverts to its original form and repairs all damage, the subject will then lose their memory of interacting with the doll. After event XXX-01, it is discovered that the doll has a cognitohazard effect that makes people want to use it.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: In an addendum, event XXX-01 is described, along with an interrogation log and security tape transcript, where a guard unknowingly uses the scp to kill his boss while patrolling the anomalous item vault the object was contained in. It is investigated and found that the SCP has developed a new property while in containment, the O5 council releases a statement acknowledging the threat posed by this and suggests the development of an Emergent Properties Research Division (EPRD), in order to study the possible ‘evolution’ of anomalous properties in contained SCPs. The SCP is reclassified from safe to euclid, and containment protocols are updated

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook here is the emergent properties idea. I don’t think I’ve ever read an article that mentions SCPs ‘evolving’ new anomalous properties, and I explain it in the article as an adaptation made by the SCP in order to affect people while still in containment. I think it’s just a cool new thing to add to the lore, as well as creating a new branch of the foundation in the EPRD

Additional Notes: As mentioned in the title, I am a first time writer, so all criticism is welcome. I’ve been reading SCPs for years so I think I have a grasp on how to write them, but we’ll see how this is received. I have the full article written in my sandbox if you’d like to just read it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: The Stalker (Looking for Green Light)
item.description: A SCP that is always around a present
item.content:encoded:
A SCP that is always around a present, first you just saw it once at work, now no matter where you are it is always there.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Emotional

Elevator Pitch: The idea is a SCP that slowly creeps into the victim's life. At first he’s a random face in the street, not unlike the hundreds of unknown faces you pass everyday. But over time he's just there more often, now he's at the commissary, at your favorite restaurant, and you swear you saw him through your front window. Wait was he that person you just saw out the corner of your eye? This process then repeats but quicker with hearing him everywhere and then even quicker with feeling his presence everywhere. After this it seems he's not only around you at all times, but now he's in your head. Every moment, every thought he's there.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP article will be told through a series of interviews and documents. The central story is a chronological story told by a series of interviews and other documents. It starts with a victim recounting his story as defined in the hook below, and then followed by his missing papers. This man is the first known victim of the SCP and causes the SCP foundation to launch an operation into the man's town to try and find the SCP (told through a OPORD). While they do find the SCP it escapes by unknown means but one of the SCP agents gets infected by the SCP and is put into quarantine. After a month in quarantine being a SCP scientist checking on the Agent is infected and the Agent seemingly disappeared. (see additional notes below) The infected scientist escapes to the original victim's town, the rest of the story is researching and testing why the SCP is attracted to here.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook will be an interview between a SCP Scientist and a SCP victim. In the interview the victim, clearly traumatized by what's happening to him, recounts his story of how the SCP is everywhere. It's basically the elevator pitch in more detail and in more detail.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure if this is similar to any other SCP, please tell me if it is. Note the final step after the SCP is always present in the victim's mind is eventually the victim becomes the SCP, still the same person, but now that person is the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Much of the history of the 20th's century was shaped by the advent of air power. But what if air power was never a thing? Air craft carriers, strategic bombing, mail by air, even tourism would all completely change. This SCP will examine ways such a world might work.

Additional Notes: I've had this idea for a couple of years now, but I was never sure what to do with it. Recently, I remembered that there's a verse in the Quran that says:

"O assembly of jinns and men! If you have power to pass beyond the zones of the heavens and the earth, then pass (them)! But you will never be able to pass them, except with authority (from Allah)!"

Essentially, the cause is that in our world, God has allowed humanity to leave the heavens and earth, but in SCP-X, God has not allowed this.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs (Edited and revised)

item.content:encoded:
A mysterious restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in 19XX. The building was then contained by the Foundation.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator Pitch:

*Green Man's chefs are green faceless humanoids wearing a chef's attire.
*They are sentient and are capable of speech despite without having a mouth.
*No one knows where the kitchen is.
*They are friendly to humans and would love to talk with them.
*When being asked anything about their kitchen, they'll become agitated and reply with "no".

Central Narrative: In 19XX, a restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in Alaska. The customers said that they've never seen the kitchen nor any door leading to it.
The Foundation then secured the restaurant and sent in agents to order food and report back on what they were served. Or at least, what they think they were served.

+ show block
– hide block

An agent was able to find the kitchen. He was wandering around the restaurant and found a hallway. He went in and saw a door. But, as he was about to open the door, the agent experienced extreme paranoia and ran away. The agent said that he felt that there was a voice warning him not to come in. Every step he took closer to the door, the voice became louder.

More agents were sent into the restaurant to find the hallway. No one found it and they returned to the entrance of the restaurant. But, 2 agents weren't present. After a couple of minutes, one of the agents was found. He was shaking in fear. The agent was asked on what happened. He said that he and the other agent found the door. They both went in despite the voice telling them not to come in. What the agent saw was terrifying. The second agent was then stabbed by one of the chefs and the agent managed to run away. Just when the agent was about to say what was the terrifying thing he saw, a chef appeared and ran towards the agent. The chef started to repeatedly stab him while [REDACTED]. More chefs appeared and they became aggressive to the other agents. The chefs chased all of them out of the restaurant. After the team managed to exit the restaurant, a closed sign appeared outside the door. The sign read "CLOSED. We are making adjustments to give you the best service".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These entities can cook delicious food with unknown ingredients. The kitchen was never seen so it remains a mystery on how these entities make the food.

  • Its an anomalous coin that will reveal 3 different sides when flipped over. The 3rd side is anomalous.
  • When the coin lands on the 3rd side it transforms whoever flipped it into a monster.
  • In addition if someone keeps the coin for a long time it will alter their behavior, making them kinda crazy but in a fun way.

Central Narrative: The coins most interesting part isn't the monster but more so what it does to the people in possession of it. It makes them more exuberant, more fond of games and gambling, risk, chaos, but not necessarily evil. Its like the coin makes whoever is holding it chaotic neutral,
but they just happen to have a chaotic evil toy in their pocket, so they're dangerous. The tales will focused less on the coin itself but more on the people its effecting.

Hook: The characters. The concept can be used pretty easily to create stories. The idea that this coin is just floating around and anybody can have it allows people to come up with their own interpretation of how the coin might corrupt someone. Plus the monster is pretty badass too in my opinion.

Notes: Sorry this first post is a little messy. It was my first post in the forum and you can get a better overall idea of what the SCP is all about by reading further in the thread, particularly my first comment below is kinda an addendum to this original post.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Epstein didn't kill himself
item.description: The surveillance footage from Epstein's cell is anti-memetic
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Modern events

+ show block
– hide block

Page Layout (Optional):

Special Containment Procedures: A copy of the scp is kept on hard drive kept in safe.

Description: Video is antimemetic. Foundation wants to know what happened in the video because Epstein was already on their radar for potential ties to a redacted GOI. Research with dangerous z-class mnestics was recently authorized

Document #XXXX-01: letter of authorization

Document #XXXX-02: Report on research with z class mnestics sent to O5. Contains test log with dialogue. Reveals that Epstein was murdered.

Document #XXXX-03: Internal document from O5 council. They believe that it was MC&D. Now they want to use that info to the advantage of the foundation.

Elevator Pitch: The surveillance feed of Epstein's death is anti-memetic. The SCP foundation wants to uncover the mystery of what happened as well as why it was covered up.

Central Narrative: Starting with the Description, I'm going to build a sense of an imposing conspiracy regarding Epstein's death. I will do this by hinting that Epstein was already on the Foundation's radar for being tied to a redacted GOI. I'm going to then hype up the efficacy of z-class mnestics by having their usage require authorization from the O5 council. Using Z-class mnestics as a benchmark, I'm gonna emphasize how extremely anti-memetic the footage. However, the testing will ultimately pull through and reveal that Epstein was murdered. Finally, in a post climax reveal, an internal document from the O5 council will reveal who they bbelieve murdered Epstein, tying back to the redacted GOI from earlier: Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP focuses on modern conspiracies that I imagine everyone on the SCP wiki are familiar with (and maybe even buy into).

Additional Notes: I know that writing an article about Epstein requires care. If I make things to political, I can drive out half of the readers. I also have to make sure remain respectful to his victims. I'm aware of that responsibility and I won't post an article unless I'm confident that I satisfy both of those benchmarks.

item.title: The Man Who Snorts Video Games, Books and Movies Like Cocaine
item.description: A cokehead decides to snort more than just cocaine...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I have no clue

Elevator Pitch:

  • A cokehead grows ashamed of himself one day and decided to smash a few of his video games. He gets the bright idea to snort the fragments and discovers that doing so gives him a signifcantly weaker version of the main character's powers/skills/abilities/etc.
  • Example: snorting Super Mario Bros lets him jump 18 feet in the air. The catch? He'll break his ankles when he lands.
+What the heck did I just write...?
-Uhh....

Central Narrative:

  • After spending much of his life disappointing his family, friends and divorced spouse, he goes on a downward spiral and then discovers his anomalous ability.
  • At first, he tries to do good.
  • He tries to help an old lady cross the road by snorting Super Mario Bros, picking her up and jumping across the street. It doesn't end well.
  • Then he snorts Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and gets the Master Sword. He attempts to stop a bank robbery. However, he has no formal sword training and ends up dropping it, firing the Master Sword energy beam and accidentally killing someone's dog. The robbers then kick his ass and leave.
  • He finally decides to go down the road of villainy instead.
  • He snorts a copy of Megaman and tries to rob a bank. He ends up burning his hand off because it turns out human flesh isn't made to rapid fire concentrated plasma shots.
  • The Foundation finally notices him and tries to contain him.
  • He snorts a copy of Grand Theft Auto and tries to steal a car.
  • Well, he steals a car, alright.
  • He can't drive and ends up crashing into a fire hydrant.
  • The Foundation catch up to him.
  • Turns out, he kept a secret weapon all him all along; it's a little glass vial filled with fragments of a copy of Persona 5. He snorts it, magically dons a really beat up, low quality edgy black trenchcoat that smells like it hasn't been washed since Persona 1's release date.
  • He tries to summon Arsene and all he gets is a floating top hat that fires a tiny glob of darkness. All it does it make the Foundation Agent sneeze.
  • He gets contained.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Um. Well. He snorts things.

Additional Notes:

Possible copyright issues? I forgot to give a movie and book as an example. Oh well.
